tools.description: Spawn a leaf agent in its own worktree and branch. The agent gets dev role (files PR, cannot spawn children). The TL worktree must be clean before spawning because dev-leaves fork from branch HEAD and cannot see uncommitted scaffold. Agent type defaults to the server config; pass agent_type only when this leaf needs a specific supported runtime. Use structured fields (steps, verify, boundary) for precise specs, or put everything in task for simple cases. Claude Code parents should create a team using TeamCreate before spawning Claude Code leaves. After spawning, return immediately.

agent_type.description: Agent type for the leaf: 'claude', 'opencode', or 'codex'. Omit to use the server default.

model.description: Optional model override, separate from agent_type.

boundary.description: DO NOT rules for known failure modes

context.description: Freeform context: code snippets, examples, patterns to follow

intent_id.description: Controller dispatch intent identifier used to correlate agent.spawned confirmation.

read_first.description: File paths to read before starting (CLAUDE.md, source patterns)

steps.description: Numbered implementation steps with code snippets and exact file paths

task.description: What to build. Combined with steps/verify/boundary into structured spec

tools.name: spawn_leaf

tools.description: Spawn an ephemeral worker in a tmux pane. The worker runs in YOUR directory on YOUR branch — no isolation, no PR, so the TL worktree must be clean before spawning. Commit the scaffold or discard throwaway output before retrying. Workers are sequential per TL tab; wait for the active worker handoff before spawning another worker, or use spawn_leaf for parallel PR work. Agent type defaults to the server config; pass agent_type only when this worker needs a specific supported runtime. PREFER WORKERS OVER DOING WORK YOURSELF — worker tokens cost far less than TL tokens. Put everything in the task string: context, instructions, file paths, anti-patterns. Workers send results via notify_parent. Claude Code parents should create a team using TeamCreate before spawning Claude Code workers. After spawning, return immediately.

agent_type.description: Agent type for the worker: 'claude', 'opencode', or 'codex'. Omit to use the server default.

model.description: Optional model override, separate from agent_type.

intent_id.description: Controller dispatch intent identifier used to correlate agent.spawned confirmation.

task.description: The full prompt. Everything the worker needs in one string

tools.description: With human approval, reset the review cycle for an existing open and unmerged PR. Clears watcher flags, disposes reviewer resources, and lets the next watcher poll spawn a fresh reviewer without renaming or disposing the author worktree. For a closed PR, use replace_close_pr instead.

pr_number.description: Open and unmerged PR number whose review cycle should be restarted after human approval

tools.description: With human approval, replace an open or closed and unmerged Forgejo PR while continuing the existing open Chainlink issue. Retires the old reviewer and author resources, preserves the old PR head SHA, and starts a fresh leaf and branch targeting the old PR base. This tool does not close the old PR; after verifying the replacement, explicitly reconcile or close it. Never use this for a merged PR.

agent_type.description: Optional fresh leaf runtime: claude, retired, shoal, opencode, or codex

chainlink_issue_id.description: Positive open Chainlink issue id to continue

replacement_task.description: Complete task for the fresh leaf, including acceptance criteria

tools.name: replace_close_pr

tools.description: Resume an existing open, unmerged PR by number. The host re-fetches its head SHA, resolves the exact owning agent, branch, and runtime, starts a fresh invocation, and verifies its exact tmux target is ready before reporting success. An already-running owner is an explicit failure, not a fresh resume. Provide the task summary plus optional read_first, steps, verify, boundary, context, and done_criteria fields for a complete review-fix handoff. On the resumed owner's next `file_pr` call, preserve or update the PR body with the literal heading `## Acceptance Criteria` and copy every issue Definition-of-Done bullet verbatim beneath it; use done_criteria as the handoff source and do not silently drop or paraphrase the heading. Never provide a leaf name or agent type. For closed or unrecoverable PRs, use the human-approved replace_close_pr workflow.

boundary.description: Constraints and anti-patterns for the repair

context.description: Reviewer analysis, root cause, proposed solution, and relevant snippets

done_criteria.description: Issue Definition-of-Done bullets for the repair; the resumed owner must copy them verbatim beneath the literal `## Acceptance Criteria` heading in the next file_pr body

pr_number.description: Existing open, unmerged PR number to resume

read_first.description: Exact files or documents the leaf must read before editing

steps.description: Concrete implementation steps for the repair

task.description: Task summary for the owning agent to continue on the existing PR

verify.description: Exact commands the leaf must run before reporting completion

Pass chainlink_issue_id to close the issue and commit CHANGELOG.md before the merge. After merging, verify the build — especially when merging multiple PRs in parallel, as changes may interact.
